speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) which industries find it difficult to attract or hire PMET Singaporeans; (b) what has been the success of initiatives of Singaporeans and local employers to address or improve the status quo in these industries; and (c) for PMET jobs held by foreigners and PRs arising from the lack of qualified Singaporeans to fill these positions, how does the Government monitor and track the skills transfer to, and the skills acquisition by, Singaporeans from PRs and foreigners over time.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Growth Sectors Initiative covers the four sectors which I mentioned earlier, as well as finance and insurance services, wholesale trade and healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked about the success of our efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have helped locals take up a wide range of jobs, including data analysts, digital advertising professionals and technical sales engineers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: PCP participants, such as Effandi Sajari, often have inspiring stories.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Effandi spent close to two decades in the energy and power sector managing projects that involved installing low voltage power network equipment across the island.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In his 40s, he wanted a change in environment and to challenge himself.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, through the PCP for Electronics Assistant Engineer, he joined GlobalFoundries as a Senior Associate Engineer.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He manages clean-room equipment to ensure optimal levels of humidity, temperature and pressure for wafer fabrication.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He now earns about 10% more than at his previous job.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Every day, we continue to help jobseekers like Effandi secure good jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On the Member's last question, the employment outcomes of our university and polytechnic graduates are a good indicator of whether we are helping Singaporeans acquire skills for PMET jobs in demand.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Based on the latest Graduate Employment Survey, around nine in 10 university and polytechnic graduates who entered the labour force were employed within six months after graduation or completion of their full-time National Service.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This figure has remained stable over the past decade.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mature workers who have been in the workforce for some time have also made good progress.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is evident when we compare the education and employment profile of local workers aged 40 and over.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: About one in four of them joined the workforce with a local diploma or degree and could have been expected to perform PMET jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But, in fact, about double, or one in two of these workers, are today holding PMET jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Overall, the number and share of employed locals in PMET employment have risen steadily over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If we look at Singapore Citizens only, the trend is very similar.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To sustain them, we must be able to continue the momentum of good job creation, motivate individuals to upskill or reskill, promote employer commitment to fair hiring and progression, and sustain Government investments in education and training.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To help Singaporeans, we must make every effort to keep up these efforts instead of focusing narrowly on displacing Permanent Residents and foreigners in our workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That would be a zero-sum game which will cause companies to rethink locating their high value activities in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The end result will not serve Singapore and Singaporeans' best interests.
